start.q: What do we need to start a project?
start.p1: We begin with your 3D-model or drawings and a brief describing the mood, materials, and goals of your project. Using our structured onboarding system, our team refines your model and translates all inputs into high-end visuals.
start.linkText: See the full list of what we need

workflow.intro: Each project goes through the following key stages:

steps.title: Discovery Stage
steps.desc: The client provides all necessary input materials. At this stage, we also prepare a cost estimate and a project timeline.

steps.title: Modeling & Optimization
steps.desc: We create or refine the 3D model based on all provided drawings and references, ensuring accuracy and efficiency for the visualization process.

steps.title: Cameras & Atmosphere Setup
steps.desc: We produce greyscale renderings to define and approve the best camera angles and overall atmosphere for your project.

steps.title: Color Previews
steps.desc: The client receives fully textured and colored renders with the selected views and atmosphere. We collect all feedback at this stage and prepare the images for final rendering.

steps.title: Final High-End Images
steps.desc: The client receives high-resolution final visualizations ready for presentations, marketing, and publications.

duration.q: How long does a project take?
paragraphs: The project timeline is always individual and depends on its complexity, goals, scale, input quality, response speed, and many other factors.
Smaller projects usually take around 7 working days, although the first drafts are typically delivered within the first few days after kickoff.

We understand that deadlines are often tight, so we organize our team efficiently to deliver as quickly as possible while keeping the entire process transparent and well-communicated with daily updates.
Before starting, every client receives a preliminary schedule outlining all key stages and we strictly follow it throughout the collaboration.

Our pricing depends on the project type (exterior or interior visualizations, animations, 360° tours, etc.), its goals, scale, and deadlines. We offer flexible pricing and prepare a custom offer for each project before we begin.
In addition, we have a clear partnership discount program for both new and returning clients designed to create long-term, mutually beneficial collaboration.

gallery.title: Gallery

All.label: All Projects
All.desc: A curated cross-section of the studio's architectural visualisation: exterior and interior renderings, aerial views, animations and cinemagraphs for residential developments, conversions and competitions in Switzerland, Germany and Austria, shown side by side. Product visualisation, virtual staging and the 360° tours have their own sections.

Exterior.label: Exterior
Exterior.desc: Photorealistic exterior visualisations of apartment buildings, villas, conversions and public buildings in their real surroundings — street views, courtyards and evening moods for sales brochures, project websites and building permits. Every image is rendered from the architect's plans or model with the specified facade materials.

Interior.label: Interior
Interior.desc: Interior renderings of living rooms, kitchens, bedrooms and bathrooms at eye level, furnished for the buyer the project is aimed at and built from the finish schedule — the show apartment for developments sold off-plan, and the base for 360° tours of the same rooms.

Bird's-Eye View.label: Bird's-Eye View
Bird's-Eye View.desc: Aerial and drone-perspective renderings that place a development in its district: terrain from elevation data, neighbours from satellite and drone imagery, the project itself at true height. Used as brochure covers, construction-site banners and neutral permit views.

Product.label: Product
Product.desc: Studio-quality product visualisation of kitchens, furniture, fittings and materials from CAD data — packshots on white and lifestyle scenes in styled interiors, with every colour and material variant rendered from one setup for catalogues, web shops and trade fairs.

Virtual Staging.label: Virtual Staging
Virtual Staging.desc: Real photographs of empty rooms furnished digitally at correct scale and light, delivered with the original and the 'virtually staged' note the portals expect — and renovation variants that show new floors, kitchens and walls in the existing room, as before-and-after pairs.

360° Tours.label: 360° Tours
360° Tours.desc: Walkable 360° tours rendered from the same scenes as the stills: drag to look around, follow the hotspots or the floor plan from room to room, on a phone, a desktop or a VR headset. The show apartment for projects that are still on paper.

Animation.label: Animation
Animation.desc: Architectural animations and mood films: camera flights from the quarter into the apartment, people, traffic and the light of a particular hour, cut for websites, sales events and social media. Each film comes from the same model as the project's renderings.

Cinemagraph.label: Cinemagraph
Cinemagraph.desc: Still renderings with one living detail in a seamless loop — a fireplace, rain on the window, curtains in a breeze — that stop the scroll in a feed and replace a hero video at a tenth of the file size.

Web.label: Web
Web.desc: Project websites, portfolios and landing pages built around the renderings: unit tables, floor plans, embedded tours and enquiry forms that name the unit, in German and English — shown here as device mockups of three example sites.
